title: Twin-Study Simulator
summary: Students set the true variance components, generate fictional twin and sibling pairs from them, and recover ACE estimates with Falconer's formulae — then switch on unequal environments, assortative mating and gene-environment correlation and watch the estimates fail in opposite directions while the truth stays put.
learningObjectives: State what heritability is a property of: variance in a population under particular environmental conditions.
Explain why heritability says nothing about the causes of any individual's trait, and nothing about malleability.
Derive ACE estimates from MZ and DZ correlations using Falconer's formulae.
Name the assumptions the derivation rests on and say which direction each violation biases the estimate.
Explain why equalising environments raises heritability without any genetic change.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every calculation runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person or their family.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, number input and buttons throughout; every slider announces a meaningful value ('assumption held' rather than '0'). The three scatterplots are hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table of pair counts and correlations, and each panel's correlation is also printed as text. The truth-against-estimate table labels every discrepancy 'overestimate', 'underestimate' or 'close' in words. The random seed is exposed so a demonstration is exactly reproducible. Changes announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Behaviour genetics: what heritability is a property of, and which way each broken assumption bends the estimate
simulationNotes: Fictional pairs from a seeded mulberry32 generator; 250 pairs per group. Phenotype is a*A + c*C + e*E + m*M with independent standard-normal sources; pair resemblance is produced by the proportion of A and C the pair shares. Estimates use Falconer's formulae. No trait is named and no real study, family or dataset is represented. The model is purely additive: no dominance, epistasis, sex differences, age moderation or gene-environment interaction (gene-environment correlation is modelled). No group comparison of any kind is simulated, and the simulation contains a single undifferentiated population.
